draft_passage: "Only if you're buying."
source_has: "Wanna get a bite to eat before you hole yourself in your apartment for the weekend?" … I grinned. "Only if you're buying."
why_damaged: In the draft Heather's dinner invitation and the narrator's grin are both cut, so the reply "Only if you're buying" appears without any preceding offer to attach to.

draft_passage: "I don't think this is going to work, Heth. She's on to me." "Anyway, nice to have met you." He walked off.
source_has: He shook his head. "It's nothing. Anyway, nice to have met you."
why_damaged: The source specifies Blake shook his head (a definite physical gesture tied to his dismissal of Heather's "On to you?" question); the draft drops both the head-shake and Heather's puzzled "On to you?" follow-up, so his exit loses its interactional grounding.

draft_passage: "Then I won't take 'no' for an answer next time. Live a little, Miriam, before your whole life is gone."
source_has: I winced. "It's not that. It's just-well, I just don't feel like I fit in. Like I'm an outsider or something, you know what I mean?" Heather shook her head. "No, and I won't take 'no' for an answer…"
why_damaged: The source's "No" is Heather directly rejecting the narrator's self-deprecating excuse; the draft drops that exchange, so "I won't take 'no' for an answer" floats without a prior refusal or request it is overriding.

draft_passage: "For the risk it'll be extra," he said.
source_has: Heather squealed and clapped her hands. "You think you can lose 'em?" The driver grinned. "No problem, but for the risk it'll be extra."
why_damaged: The draft keeps Heather's question but cuts the driver's confident "No problem" affirmative before the price caveat, and more critically the driver's line now reads as a spontaneous condition rather than a reply to her specific can-you-lose-them question since the grin and direct answer are removed.

draft_passage: "Wait! Where are you going?"
source_has: I staggered past her and down the alley that we'd come. Heather reached out for me. "Hey, wait! Where are you going?"
why_damaged: The draft removes "Heather reached out for me" and the "Hey" address, so her question appears without the physical reaching-out that constitutes the stimulus she is responding to.

draft_passage: Its only reaction was tears that pooled in my eyes and slid down my cheeks.
source_has: My body still wouldn't respond. Its only reaction was tears…
why_damaged: The draft cuts "My body still wouldn't respond" immediately before this sentence, leaving the antecedent of "Its" absent; a reader cannot tell from the draft alone what "its" refers to.

draft_passage: "See? I get results," she smirked.
source_has: "Will you stop that?" one of the women to my left snapped. "You've been trying that for fifteen minutes..." — Mascara-face sneered at her. "You idiots can just sit there, but I'm not going to give up."
why_damaged: The draft cuts the exchange where another woman rebukes Mascara-face and Mascara-face defies her before shouting for help, so her triumphant "See? I get results" has no adversarial audience to be directed at and reads as unprompted self-congratulation rather than a pointed retort.

draft_passage: Blake's snout-nosed face peered in.
source_has: "The fake flesh that clung tightly to his brown skin" was removed in ch.2; in ch.3 source says "revealed Blake in all his piggy glory" — the unmasked face is the reader's second sighting.
why_damaged: The draft ch.6 (source ch.2) shows Blake removing a prosthetic mask in Miriam's apartment, but the draft of that scene keeps the mask-removal without clearly establishing Blake's true face for the reader; when the draft ch.7 then presents "Blake's snout-nosed face" at the truck with no qualifier, the reader of the draft alone has not had a prior clear description of the snouted face to recognise as the same revealed feature.

draft_passage: She wiped her face. "W-where are they taking us? Why did they take us?"
source_has: "She looked up at me. 'You okay?' The girl shook her head. She wiped her face and swallowed. 'W-where are they taking us?'"
why_damaged: The draft drops "She looked up at me" and the head-shake, so the girl's spoken reply loses its interactional anchor — the reader cannot see that the wiping and speaking are responses to Miriam's direct question and the girl's prior nonverbal answer.

draft_passage: "That's enough. We're not getting anywhere with this arguing," another woman said.
source_has: Source has a full back-and-forth: Miriam tells Olivia "we should stick together," Olivia says she won't drag a brat, Miriam invokes "pig boys," Olivia retorts "it's everybody for themselves" and criticises the group for not making noise with her — only then does the fifth woman intervene.
why_damaged: The draft omits Olivia's "everybody for themselves" speech and her accusation that no one helped her make noise, so the fifth woman's "we're not getting anywhere" mediating intervention has no full escalating quarrel to logically interrupt.

draft_passage: "We just want to go home!" one of the other women cried.
source_has: "But we just want to go home!" — source attributes this line as "one of the women yelled" in a four-line volley distinct from Stephanie's and Alex's lines that follow.
why_damaged: The draft has already given Stephanie and Alex named lines in the same exchange; without explicit attribution this line blurs into either of them, obscuring that a third, unnamed captive also joins the chorus.

draft_passage: Blake bared his teeth and took a step. The woman raised a hand. He stopped cold.
source_has: "But I just want to go home," Stephanie insisted. Blake took a step toward her and curled his lips back. "I told you, you can't go back, now-" The woman raised her hand.
why_damaged: In the draft Blake's aggressive step and the woman's silencing gesture appear unmotivated because Stephanie's plea and Blake's verbal lunge at her have been cut, removing the stimulus the woman is reacting to.

draft_passage: Alex inched close, murmuring something soft.
source_has: Alex wiggled up beside her and smiled. "It'll be okay."
why_damaged: The draft replaces Alex's direct reassurance with a vague action ('murmuring something soft'), so the reader cannot determine who spoke or what was said, losing the clear attribution the source provides.

draft_passage: I met those green eyes without blinking.
source_has: I met his red eyes without blinking.
why_damaged: Beyond the eye-colour discrepancy, the draft describes the Grand Dragon Lord's eyes as green throughout, yet the source specifically names them red at this charged confrontational moment; the draft's 'green' creates a contradiction the reader cannot resolve from draft context alone, obscuring whose gaze Miriam is holding.

draft_passage: The lord said, half-turning. To Blake: "Unchain my Maiden."
source_has: The dragon lord half-turned to him. "Then she will suit me." His eyes flickered to Blake.
why_damaged: The draft's 'half-turning' has no specified object, so it is unclear whether the lord is turning toward Renner, Blake, or Miriam; the source makes explicit he half-turns to Renner before then redirecting his gaze to Blake.

draft_passage: "Take her away," he said.
source_has: The lord turned to his adviser. "Have her taken to her new quarters." Renner's shriveled shoulders slumped. He sighed and bowed his head. "As you wish, My Lord." He clapped his hands. A pair of guards… He nodded at me. "Take her away."
why_damaged: The draft omits Renner's explicit compliance ('As you wish') and his nod directing the guards to Miriam, so 'Take her away' floats without the clear chain of command—lord's order → adviser's relay → guards' trigger—that the source establishes.

draft_passage:
"Should we check the lord's room?"
"It must be done, but quietly," she replied to someone.
source_has: "Should we check the lord's room?" a man's voice wondered. / "It must be done, but quietly," the old woman replied.
why_damaged: In the draft both lines are given to the old woman ('she replied to someone'), making her ask and answer her own question, whereas the source assigns the first line to an unnamed male servant.

draft_passage: but the girl has once again escaped
source_has: but the girl has once again escaped
why_damaged: The draft's Chapter 7 opens with the narrator waking in the room for the first time; no prior escape attempt has been shown in the draft's Chapter 7, so 'once again' has no referent within the draft's own N+1 chapter (the earlier escape is in N but is the narrator's first flight, not a second one the old woman could call 'once again').

draft_passage: I froze as the color drained from my face. "She did what to me?"
source_has: He pursed his lips and those red eyes of his felt as though they looked into my soul. "You don't understand. The Lady of the Pond granted you a gift…" / I froze and felt the color drain from my face. "She did what to me?"
why_damaged: In the draft the Lord's warning about the Lady's gift and the danger of leaving is run together without the beat of the narrator's 'I froze' being separated from it; more critically, the draft merges his two separate speeches into one unbroken paragraph, removing the paragraph break that signalled her stunned reaction as a response to a complete statement, making the freeze-and-question feel like it interrupts rather than answers the Lord's remark.

draft_passage: He shuddered, jaw tight.
source_has: I petted the wing with one hand. It twitched beneath my fingers… The lord shut his eyes and ground his teeth together.
why_damaged: The draft cuts the narrator's act of petting the wing, so the lord's shudder/jaw-clench has no visible stimulus to react to in the draft.

draft_passage: "Are you all right?"
source_has: His breathing came out in quick gasps, and he appeared in pain. 'Are you allright?'
why_damaged: The draft removed the narrator's observation that he appeared to be in pain, so her concern-question floats without the visual cue that prompted it.

draft_passage: "Should we check the lord's room?" … "It must be done, but quietly," she replied to someone.
source_has: "Should we check the lord's room?" a man's voice wondered. "It must be done, but quietly," the old woman replied.
why_damaged: The draft attributes the first line only as a drifting voice and drops 'a man's voice wondered', leaving the exchange's two distinct speakers (unnamed man vs. old woman) indistinguishable from the old woman speaking both lines.

draft_passage: but the girl has once again escaped
source_has: the girl has once again escaped
why_damaged: The draft's compressed opening skips the source Chapter 6 context of a prior escape, and within this draft chapter there is no earlier escape attempt recounted before the old woman says 'once again', making the 'again' a first occurrence.

draft_passage: His face softened as he studied mine.
source_has: His face softened as he studied mine.
why_damaged: Not flagged — source also uses the bare 'softened' without a specified object, so draft matches source exactly here.

draft_passage: "Hungry," he diagnosed.
source_has: The lord's eyes opened, and he smiled at me. "So it seems."
why_damaged: The draft replaces "So it seems" with "Hungry," he diagnosed" — a new paraphrase that is adequately attributed — but the immediately preceding exchange cuts the narrator's line "I'm kind of hungry" and the stomach growl lands before he speaks, so the reader cannot tell whether he is diagnosing her stomach or her words; however the deeper problem is the next flag.

draft_passage: He chuckled. "That you still hide yourself from me after such an intimate act."
source_has: He chuckled, and I glared at him. 'What's so funny?' He nodded at my hands. 'That you still hide yourself…'
why_damaged: The draft cuts the narrator's question "What's so funny?" and the lord's gesture toward her hands, so his spoken line has no interrogative prompt and reads as an incomplete, unmotivated sentence fragment rather than an answer.

draft_passage: His eyes flicked, and he smiled. "They have ample assets."
source_has: "So, what do the female dragons get?" I asked him. His eyes wandered down to my breasts. 'They have ample assets.'
why_damaged: The draft retains "So what do the females get?" so the reply is prompted — this is a near-miss — but "His eyes flicked" replaces the source's directed gaze "His eyes wandered down to my breasts," making the smile appear unmotivated and the innuendo of the answer opaque.

draft_passage: His eyes flicked, and he smiled.
source_has: His eyes wandered down to my breasts.
why_damaged: The source specifies exactly where his eyes move and why (the innuendo that explains "ample assets"), but the draft's bare "his eyes flicked" strips the directional object, leaving the reader unable to infer what he is reacting to.

draft_passage: He sighed. "I warned you before: I can find you anywhere in this world. You are no longer hidden from my Second Sight. The Marking ensured that."
source_has: "I warned you before that I can find you anywhere in this world."
why_damaged: The draft retains the back-reference "I warned you before" but Chapter N+1's draft contains no prior warning about the Second Sight or the Marking, so the callback to an earlier promise has no anchor within the draft text the reader has seen.

draft_passage: I wanted only to pleasure and be pleasured. This man could pleasure me, could take me and claim me again and again.
source_has: Source uses "again and again" in the same sentence as part of the narrator's lust-haze interior monologue.
why_damaged: The draft has compressed the earlier sexual encounter so heavily (no described repeated strokes or second climax before this line) that "again and again" has no prior occurrence within the draft to repeat, making the iteration read as floating.

draft_passage: "Then he got Stephanie?" I said, remembering the bargain I'd struck in panic.
source_has: I blinked at him for a moment before I remembered my 'sacrifice' to Stephanie.
why_damaged: The draft's parenthetical "the bargain I'd struck in panic" replaces the source's
Stephanie,: ut Chapter N's draft never depicts or names any bargain or sacrifice involving Stephanie, so the pronoun-anchored interior reference has no established antecedent for a reader of the draft alone.

draft_passage: "I'm afraid I'm not familiar with that term."
source_has: The dragon lord shook his head. "I'm afraid I'm not familiar with that term."
why_damaged: The draft has dropped the attribution tag and the immediately preceding speaker was the narrator (Miriam), so a reader cannot be certain whether Xander or Cayden is answering her 'frat party' question.

draft_passage: "It's where guys get together and prove how manly they are by drinking and eating a lot."
source_has: I sighed. "It's where guys get together and prove how manly they are by drinking and eating a lot."
why_damaged: The source tags this line to Miriam with 'I sighed'; the draft strips that beat, leaving two consecutive untagged lines in a four-person scene where attribution is not recoverable from context alone.

draft_passage: Cayden drew breath to object, but Xander lifted a hand and he fell silent.
source_has: Cayden glanced at my dragon lord and pursed his lips. "I think maybe we should call-" Xander raised his hand and silenced the younger lord.
why_damaged: The draft cuts Cayden's actual spoken objection, so the reader sees him silenced before any stimulus—the 'object' is described but its content (the thing being interrupted) has been removed, making the silencing action hang without the interactional trigger it responds to.

draft_passage: "I'd prefer your wings off me so I can find my clothes and try to escape again."
source_has: Source ch 9 draft opens the chapter mid-scene; no prior escape attempt appears anywhere in the draft of ch 13.
why_damaged: The word 'again' presupposes a previous escape attempt the reader can point to within the draft, but ch 13's draft contains no earlier scene of escape, so 'again' floats without an antecedent event.

draft_passage: "That you are not enjoying the ride as much as I would wish."
source_has: "That you are not enjoying the ride as much as I would wish," he commented.
why_damaged: The draft drops the narrator's preceding line "What do you think?" as a clear rhetorical question that still survives, so the stimulus is present — but the draft also drops Xander's speech tag, making this line float without a speaker; however the deeper problem is the next exchange: see below.

draft_passage: "You don't exactly come with a seat belt or parachute."
source_has: I glanced down at the earth far below us. "You don't exactly come with a seat belt or parachute."
why_damaged: The draft removes the narration beat that attributes this line to Miriam; after Xander's untagged comment above it, the speaker of this line is ambiguous.

draft_passage: "Promise me you will remain here." I pressed my lips together and nodded.
source_has: "Promise me you will remain here." I pursed my lips but nodded. He smiled. "Then wait for me. I will return."
why_damaged: The draft keeps the promise-and-nod but cuts Xander's follow-up "Then wait for me. I will return," which is the payoff line the promise-exchange is building toward and which the reader needs to feel the weight of his departure.

draft_passage: His voice softened. "Promise me you will remain here."
source_has: Source has no softening tag here; the draft has inserted a bare "softened" without a definitional object — the source simply has him speak the line.
why_damaged: The draft adds "His voice softened" as a bare vague verb with no object (softened how — in tone, in volume, in urgency?) where the source had no such tag, creating a new vague-reaction-verb artifact rather than compressing one.

draft_passage: He drew me and Stephanie shoulder to shoulder, then gripped my shoulders and met my eyes.
source_has: His hands at his sides lengthened into sharp claws. He pulled me to the side and Cayden did the same with Stephanie, so we stood shoulder-to-shoulder. Xander turned to me and grasped my shoulders.
why_damaged: The draft has just named both Xander and Cayden in adjacent sentences; "He drew me and Stephanie shoulder to shoulder" is ambiguous as to whether Xander or Cayden is performing the action, whereas the source explicitly names Xander at the equivalent moment.

draft_passage: Cayden tore himself from Stephanie's grasp and, shrinking from man to gold-scaled beast, followed.
source_has: Cayden reluctantly separated himself from Stephanie and took Xander's empty place. He, too, transformed into a majestic dragon.
why_damaged: The draft uses "shrinking" to describe Cayden's transformation, but earlier in the draft his transformation was never shown to the reader (only Xander's was described in detail in this chapter), so there is no established prior occurrence for the reader to contextualise "shrinking" as a known process for Cayden specifically.

draft_passage: "Try me."
source_has: "I'm not sure you're going to believe what I'm going to tell you." / "Try me."
why_damaged: In the draft, Heather has just commented on Miriam's clothes; 'Try me' is Heather's challenge to Miriam to tell her story, but the draft cut Miriam's preceding line ('I'm not sure you're going to believe what I'm going to tell you'), so 'Try me' appears as an unprompted non-sequitur response to a remark about Miriam's appearance.

draft_passage: "Why should you care?" she called, then brought the glasses. "It's not like you love the guy, right?"
source_has: "What the hell happened?" I whispered. "Why should you care?" Heather called from the kitchen.
why_damaged: In the draft, 'Why should you care?' has no stimulus: Miriam's whispered trigger line ('What the hell happened?') was cut, so Heather's response floats without anything to respond to.

draft_passage: "Are you even listening to me?"
source_has: "I'm not grieving!" I snapped. / She nodded at my shoulder … 'Maybe he's seriously injured, or maybe he's dying.'
why_damaged: In the source, 'Are you even listening to me?' comes after Miriam snaps 'I'm not grieving!' and Heather ignores it to speculate about Xander's injuries; the draft omitted Miriam's 'I'm not grieving!' line, so her accusation that Heather isn't listening has no suppressed protest it could be defending.

draft_passage: "He's probably got great teeth," she pointed out.
source_has: Heather walked over to the connected kitchen and wrangled about for some glasses … 'He's probably got great teeth,' she pointed out.
why_damaged: In the draft, the conversation has jumped from Miriam's 'I'll take it' directly to this line with no bridging action or attribution cue, and the preceding topic (drinking) is unrelated to dragon teeth, so it is not clear without the source's transitional narration that this is Heather continuing her matchmaking thread rather than a non-sequitur from Miriam.

draft_passage: Another hot hiss seared my shoulder. I clapped my hand over the mark.
source_has: "I was joking." Another sharp pain hit me in the shoulder.
why_damaged: The draft's earlier pain episode uses 'twinged again' to reference the first occurrence, and then calls this one 'Another hot hiss', but the intervening 'twinged again' sentence was placed in a different context (while she's asking about silver), so the word 'Another' here could work—however the real damage is that the draft also dropped the explicit first recurrence line ('I was joking. Another sharp pain') making it unclear this is the third distinct episode; a reader cannot confirm the count of prior occurrences the word 'Another' is anchoring to.

draft_passage: He turned to a gold-cloaked elder, who lifted his hand and grinned. "To the skies, before I throw you myself."
source_has: The one in the gold cloak raised his hand and shook his head. 'Do not concern yourself with apologies. We all would risk our cloaks for our lords.' He smiled and nodded at the air above us. 'Now to the skies before I throw you myself.'
why_damaged: The draft cuts Apuleius's apology and the gold-cloaked elder's response to it, so the elder's line appears to be an unprompted non-sequitur with no conversational trigger the reader can identify.

draft_passage: He turned to a gold-cloaked elder, who lifted his hand and grinned. "To the skies, before I throw you myself."
source_has: Apuleius turned to one of the gray-cloaked men. 'I will escort My Lady to My Lord.' … 'But Father Apuleius—' 'If anyone is to see My Lord to health, it shall be his Lady,' Apuleius told him. He glanced at the others and bowed his head. 'Please forgive me—'
why_damaged: The elder's "Do not concern yourself with apologies" (compressed to a grin) is a direct reply to Apuleius's apology and his explanation that he is bypassing protocol; the draft drops the entire exchange, so the elder's permission-granting role and the reason any permission was needed are invisible.

draft_passage: "If you will pardon my forwardness," he said—and swept me up.
source_has: 'If you will pardon my forwardness, My Lady,' he apologized. I didn't have time to ask him why before he swept me into his arms.
why_damaged: The draft's pronoun "he" immediately follows a sentence about his wings unfurling and has no named subject in the preceding clause, making it momentarily unclear whether Apuleius or an unnamed guard is speaking and acting.

draft_passage: "Why should you care?" she called, then brought the glasses. "It's not like you love the guy, right?"
source_has: "What the hell happened?" I whispered. "Why should you care?" Heather called from the kitchen.
why_damaged: The draft omits Miriam's whispered "What the hell happened?", so Heather's "Why should you care?" arrives as a reply with no audible stimulus the reader can attach it to.

draft_passage: "We cannot allow you to escape again," he said through his teeth.
source_has: Source ch 13 retains this line, and source ch 12 (the portal scene / kidnap backstory) establishes the prior escape; however the draft of ch 16 compresses the backstory to 'I was dragged into the wrong crowd' with no explicit earlier escape from the castle narrated in either draft chapter.
why_damaged: Neither draft chapter has shown or stated that Miriam previously escaped from Xander's castle, so Cayden's "again" has no referent within the draft text the reader has been given.

draft_passage: "The pleasure is all mine, My Lady," he answered without lifting his head.
source_has: She greeted him: "Dragon of the Golden Fields. It is a pleasure to meet you," — then "He didn't lift his head. 'The pleasure is all mine, My Lady.'"
why_damaged: The draft attributes the Lady's greeting line to an unintroduced 'she said' with no prior name given in the draft for the woman who just emerged; more critically, Cayden's reply verb 'answered' works, but the Lady's greeting line itself is rendered as bare dialogue with 'she said' where draft has not yet established her name — however the primary break is that the greeting speech tag reads 'she said' when 'she' in immediate prior context is ambiguous between the Lady and Miriam as the last named female actor.

draft_passage: "Because he was hurt trying to protect me," I said, swallowing the lump in my throat. "I owe him."
source_has: "I swallowed the lump in my throat. It wasn't easy being this close to such an ethereal being. 'Because he was hurt trying to protect me.'"
why_damaged: The draft duplicates 'swallowing the lump in my throat' as a tag on the spoken line, having already used the identical beat in the immediately preceding sentence ('She stopped a foot away… I couldn't move'), creating a doubled internal action with no source warrant and making the narration around the dialogue internally contradictory.

draft_passage: "Hold him," I told Cayden and the doctor. Cayden pinned his arms; Apuleius took his legs; the doctor pried his jaw.
source_has: "Could you hold him still and get his mouth open for me?" — source frames this as a question/request to which Cayden, Apuleius, and the doctor each take assigned roles.
why_damaged: The draft converts the polite request into a flat command, but more damagingly it has Apuleius taking Xander's legs without any prior re-introduction of Apuleius into the scene after the group entered the chamber — the draft's chamber description lists him nowhere, so his sudden participation in holding Xander has no interactional trigger visible to the reader.

draft_passage: A grin slid onto my face as the water gurgled. A column of water rose and burst outward.
source_has: "The familiar column of water burst into the air" — source uses 'familiar' because Ch 017 source showed Miriam previously witnessing this exact phenomenon.
why_damaged: The draft drops 'familiar,' which is acceptable compression, but the grin is the real problem: the draft has Miriam grin before anything wondrous has happened (only a ker-plop), whereas in the source the grin attaches to recognising the familiar column — without 'familiar' or any prior draft-chapter sighting of the Lady's emergence, the grin reads as an unprompted reaction to a stone splashing.

draft_passage: "The dragon form is a great strain on the body," he reminded me. "We will travel by horseback."
source_has: "No, but as I told you before the dragon form is a great strain on the body. That is why we will travel by horseback."
why_damaged: The draft cuts 'as I told you before', which anchors the reminder to a prior conversation; without it 'reminded me' has no referent in the draft — the reader has seen no earlier statement by Xander about the dragon form being a strain, so the response verb 'reminded' is unprompted.

draft_passage: A column of water rose and burst outward. The Lady stepped through, her brilliant blue eyes sliding from me to Cayden.
source_has: "The familiar column of water burst into the air"
why_damaged: The source's word 'familiar' signals this is a repeated phenomenon the narrator has witnessed before, establishing continuity with a prior chapter; the draft drops 'familiar' without substituting any earlier occurrence in the draft itself, so the sense that this is a known, recurring event is lost.

draft_passage: "The pleasure is all mine, My Lady," he answered without lifting his head.
source_has: "He didn't lift his head. 'The pleasure is all mine, My Lady.'"
why_damaged: In the draft the immediately preceding named subject is 'she' (the Lady), so 'he answered' could momentarily attach to the wrong antecedent; the source made Cayden's ongoing posture explicit before the line, removing ambiguity the draft reintroduces.

draft_passage: He let my hand go and turned his head.
source_has: "His hand fell away from mine and turned his head away from me."
why_damaged: The draft's 'turned his head' drops the directional object 'away from me', which is interactionally meaningful — it signals Xander's deliberate emotional withdrawal from Miriam in the moment of releasing her; without it the gesture is spatially and emotionally unanchored.

draft_passage: He let my hand go and turned his head.
source_has: His hand fell away from mine and turned his head away from me.
why_damaged: The draft's 'turned his head' drops 'away from me', losing the directional object that signals Xander is averting his gaze from Miriam as an interactional gesture of resignation.

draft_passage:
"But I got through."
"Yes, but you are the first. I should not consider myself an exception to a rule that has stood a thousand years."
source_has: "But I got through," I reminded him.
why_damaged: The source marks Miriam's line as a deliberate reminder of an established fact; without 'reminded him' the draft loses the interactional logic that she is invoking a prior shared witness event to challenge his reasoning, making her interjection read as a simple statement rather than a counter-argument anchored in their shared experience.

draft_passage: Any reply drowned in the weather's fresh fury. The downpour doubled, a drumbeat so loud it swallowed thought. Xander and Spiros exchanged tight looks.
source_has: What I did catch, however, was a change in their expressions. They gazed out on the rains with pursed lips and furrowed brows before they glanced at each other with knowing looks.
why_damaged: The draft replaces the source's specified 'knowing looks'—a defined interactional signal that the two men share private awareness of a threat—with the bare 'tight looks', stripping the cue that their exchange communicates unspoken mutual understanding rather than mere shared anxiety.
